title: How to Ask Wedding Guests to Share Photos: 12 Scripts
description: How to ask wedding guests to share photos: copy-paste wording for your website, invitation, signs, a 20-second announcement and the morning-after text.
dek: Copy-paste wording for every touchpoint, plus the timing that keeps it from nagging.
excerpt: Exact wording for the wedding website, invitation insert, table cards, a 20-second DJ script, the morning-after text and one follow-up, with timing and etiquette rules.

faq.q: How do you ask guests to send wedding photos without being pushy?
faq.a: Ask for their view rather than their effort (“you’ll see moments we miss”), give one link that opens without a sign-in, and say when everyone will see the album. Send one message within 48 hours of the wedding and at most one reminder about a week later. After that, let it go and thank the people who did share.

faq.q: What should I put on my wedding website about photos?
faq.a: Add an FAQ entry that answers two things at once: whether phones are welcome during the ceremony, and how to share photos at the reception. Mention the QR code on the tables and when you’ll share the album back. Three or four friendly sentences are enough; save the link itself for the day, when guests actually have photos to add.

faq.q: When should you text guests for wedding photos?
faq.a: Within 48 hours, ideally the morning after, mid-morning rather than early. The photos are still at the top of everyone’s camera roll and the night is fresh. Send one follow-up email about a week later with a closing date for the album, and stop there.

faq.q: Is it rude to ask wedding guests for their photos?
faq.a: No. Plenty of guests take photos anyway and are glad to see them used. It only becomes awkward when the ask is repeated, when guests feel they’re doing the photographer’s job, or when their photos end up somewhere public without warning. Keep the album private and say so.

faq.q: Should I put photo-sharing details on the wedding invitation?
faq.a: Keep the invitation itself for the essentials, and put one line about photos on a details card, the back of the RSVP card or your wedding website. The full instructions and the QR code belong on the day-of signs, because invitations arrive weeks ahead and usually stay at home.
